paper.title: MemQ: Integrating Q-Learning into Self-Evolving Memory Agents over Provenance DAGs
paper.central_claim: Applying TD(lambda) eligibility traces to per-memory Q-values along a provenance DAG (which records which memories were retrieved when each new memory was built) assigns multi-step credit for memory-creation chains; across five interaction/code/agentic benchmarks it improves average held-out, final runtime and cumulative success rates over the strongest baseline by 2.53, 4.23 and 2.13 pp, with ablations supporting bootstrapping and multi-depth propagation.

evidence.quote: current methods treat each memory independently, i.e., evaluating retrieval quality in isolation without accounting for the dependency chains through which memories enable the creation of future memories.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: no credit assignment across memory-creation chains.

evidence.quote: associates each vector-store entry with a Q-value and updates it by single-step exponential moving average (EMA)
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbor MemRL: per-memory Q with single-step EMA (gamma=0), run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: The unresolved gap is multi-step credit assignment across memory-creation events
evidence.support_explanation: Stated residual bottleneck; the paper does not report statistics on how often retrieved memories are themselves built from earlier retrieved memories (DAG depth/branching) to show the chains matter at scale.

evidence.quote: MemQ records retrieved parents in a provenance DAG and propagates TD errors along every backward provenance path
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: path-wise TD(lambda) credit over the provenance DAG.

evidence.quote: Here, the relevant distance is structural depth in a memory-construction graph whose edges record retrieval exposure.
evidence.support_explanation: Edges encode exposure (retrieved set -> new memory), not demonstrated causal use of the parent in producing the child.

evidence.quote: The best-epoch memory bank is selected on the memory-accumulation split before held-out evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection/evaluation split is respected for the bank epoch; per-benchmark gamma/lambda selection is not described.

evidence.quote: a closely related approach that updates per-memory utility values via single-step EMA without eligibility traces.
evidence.support_explanation: MemRL description; baselines also include No Memory, RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0, MemP.

evidence.quote: MemQ attains average held-out, final runtime, and cumulative SRs of 56.17%, 71.50%, and 78.88%, respectively
evidence.support_explanation: Headline numbers; held-out avg exceeds MemP by 2.53 pp, final SR and CSR exceed MemRL by 4.23 and 2.13 pp.

evidence.quote: occur on DSBench and AutomationBench, both using the 284B DeepSeek backbone.
evidence.support_explanation: Largest held-out margins sit on the two benchmarks where MemRL is configured with initial Q=0 versus MemQ 0.66 (Tables 16-17).

evidence.quote: 175 problems (140 train / 35 evaluation).
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out sets are small: LiveCodeBench 35, BFCL 100 test, GPQA 40, ERQA 80, DSBench 116, AutomationBench 120, LLAB 150.

evidence.quote: every method uses this split, and hyperparameters are not tuned on the held-out set.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit no-held-out-tuning statement given for LLAB only.

evidence.quote: Full MemQ achieves the highest point estimate on all three metrics across all three benchmarks
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation: gamma=0 (no bootstrap) and lambda=0 (no ancestor propagation) variants lose 2.4-8.6 pp evaluation SR on LiveCodeBench, BFCL, DSBench.

evidence.quote: These contrasting responses suggest that the benefit of longer-range credit propagation depends on the task.
evidence.support_explanation: Optimal gamma/lambda differ by benchmark (LiveCodeBench peaks near gamma 0.5 and falls at 0.9; BFCL favors 0.8-1.0).

evidence.quote: Learned Q-values are associated with subsequent task success.
evidence.support_explanation: Pearson r=0.640 over 480 AutomationBench rollouts; correlational, retrieval-time Q is itself a function of past outcomes and similarity.

evidence.quote: Parent mean gives the best evaluation SR in both benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Initialisation matters a lot: LiveCodeBench eval SR 51.43 (parent mean) vs 34.29 (init 0); BFCL 62.83 vs 57.76 (Table 6).

evidence.quote: excluding evaluation and embedding tokens
evidence.support_explanation: DSBench training tokens 313.03M +/- 40.01 (MemQ) vs 352.38M +/- 27.65 (MemRL) vs 373.35M +/- 25.78 (MemP), 3 seeds: reductions of 11-16% are within about one SD.

evidence.quote: Without extended multi-turn interaction with an environment, procedural experience from earlier tasks has fewer opportunities to guide subsequent actions.
evidence.support_explanation: On self-contained MCQ tasks margins over the strongest baseline are 0.19-0.84 pp (E024).

evidence.quote: This is also the fixed point of the depth-zero update.
evidence.support_explanation: On a fixed DAG the unique fixed point is independent of lambda, so multi-depth propagation changes convergence behaviour, not the target value; guarantees are for full-buffer updates on a fixed graph.

evidence.quote: captures synergy, redundancy, and distraction among co-retrieved memories.
evidence.support_explanation: First-order per-memory projection leaves a residual xi that is bounded in theory (Prop A.2) but never measured empirically.

evidence.quote: Successful trajectories are stored directly; after failure, an LLM produces a reflection that is stored separately.
evidence.support_explanation: Every task produces a stored memory; there is no admission gate or retirement/pruning step (Algorithm 1 only appends).

evidence.quote: To mitigate cold start, the new memory inherits the uniform mean Q-value of its retrieved parents.
evidence.support_explanation: New entries start with parents' average value, carrying prior credit forward until outcomes correct it.

evidence.quote: We use the official MemRL codebase for the MemP experiments because it has already integrated MemP.
evidence.support_explanation: MemP and RAG run inside the MemRL codebase; Self-RAG is a prompted re-implementation because released checkpoints did not work.

evidence.quote: Average across the five benchmarks is reported with approximate 95% CIs below.
evidence.support_explanation: Average held-out MemQ 56.17 [54.98, 57.37] vs MemP 53.65 [52.09, 55.20]: intervals overlap.

evidence.quote: MemQ has the highest mean on each benchmark, but its margins over the strongest baseline for each task are only 0.19, 0.83, and 0.84 pp, respectively
evidence.support_explanation: Small, undetermined-significance margins on MMMU Pro, ERQA, GPQA.

evidence.quote: Held-out SR MemQ vs strongest baseline: LLAB 74.67 vs 74.44 (MemRL); LiveCodeBench 51.43 vs 50.48 (RAG); BFCL 62.38 vs 61.39 (MemP); DSBench 47.70 vs 45.40 (Mem0); AutomationBench 44.69 vs 43.17 (MemRL); SDs 0.5-2.9
evidence.support_explanation: Our reading: per-benchmark held-out margins over the best baseline are +0.2 to +2.3 pp with SDs of 0.5-2.9, and 1 problem is 2.9 pp on LiveCodeBench, so the 8.6 pp lambda=0 ablation is about 3 problems.

evidence.quote: MemQ gamma/lambda by benchmark: LLAB 0.5/0.7; LiveCodeBench 0.3/0.95; BFCL 0.5/0.8; DSBench 0.9/0.5; AutomationBench 0.5/0.8; initial Q: MemQ 0.66 vs MemRL 0 on DSBench and AutomationBench; epochs 10-100
evidence.support_explanation: Our reading: MemQ has two extra tuned knobs per benchmark and differing initial Q from MemRL on the two benchmarks with the largest held-out gains; how knobs were selected is not stated outside LLAB.

evidence.quote: The best-performing weights identified here were not adopted in the main experiments
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval-weight sweeps are explicitly kept separate from the main configurations (point estimates).

evidence.quote: Within each benchmark, rows show final-epoch success rate (Final SR) and cumulative success rate (CSR), respectively, on the memory-accumulation split.
evidence.support_explanation: Final SR and CSR (the 4.23 and 2.13 pp headline gains) are measured on the tasks used to build the memory, i.e. training-stream performance, not held-out generalization.

signatures.object: Per-memory Q-values and a provenance DAG attached to an append-only episodic memory store used by a frozen LLM; baseline = MemRL single-step EMA Q-values and similarity-only retrieval
signatures.information: Binary task reward and trajectory from the benchmark; retrieved set A_j; newly built memory; exogenous task stream; no held-out tasks during accumulation
signatures.operation: After each batch compute delta = R + gamma*Q(m_new) - Q(m) for each retrieved memory, enumerate backward provenance paths up to depth D=4, accumulate alpha*(gamma*lambda)^|p|*delta at every ancestor with path-count normalisation, clip, flush per epoch
signatures.output: Updated Q-values used in score = w_s*sim + w_q*Q over a similarity-filtered candidate set with epsilon-greedy top-k
signatures.conditions: tasks that reuse procedural experience over multiple epochs; locality threshold theta_sim; per-benchmark gamma, lambda, weights, initial Q, epochs
signatures.feedback: task success reward (binary) and bootstrapped child memory Q
signatures.selection_rule_data: Q-guided ranking (no deletion); best-epoch memory bank chosen on the memory-accumulation split; held-out split used for evaluation
signatures.persistence: memory content + embeddings + Q + parent IDs persist across epochs; store grows monotonically
signatures.later_use: retrieval ranking on later tasks and on held-out tasks with the selected bank
signatures.claimed_effect: avg held-out 56.17 vs 53.65 (MemP), final SR 71.50 vs 67.27 (MemRL), CSR 78.88 vs 76.75 (MemRL)
signatures.failure_boundary: self-contained MCQ tasks (gains 0.2-0.8 pp); task-dependent gamma/lambda; credit assigned by exposure rather than causal use; no pruning of harmful or stale memories

signatures.object: Memory construction (proceduralization of trajectories, reflections after failure) with parent-mean Q initialisation
signatures.information: full trajectory and outcome of the current task
signatures.operation: LLM distils a 3-5 step script, stores script and raw trajectory; reflection stored separately after failure; new Q = mean of parent Q
signatures.output: new memory entry with inherited value
signatures.claimed_effect: parent-mean init beats fixed 0.5 or 0 on evaluation SR (Table 6)

gap.author_gap: Existing value-based memory methods credit only the directly retrieved memories (single-step EMA), giving earlier ancestors that enabled later memories no signal.
gap.checked_gap: Specific and well placed: MemRL is the closest prior (gamma=0 contextual-bandit update) and is run as a baseline, TD(lambda) lineage is clear. Not shown: how frequent or deep memory-creation chains are in the benchmarks (no DAG statistics), nor that the benefit comes from ancestors that were not themselves retrieved later.

claims.text: MemQ improves average held-out success over the strongest baseline
claims.setting: five interaction/code/agentic benchmarks, four different frozen backbones, memory-accumulation split + held-out split, 3 seeds
claims.baseline_control: No Memory, RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0, MemP, MemRL
claims.selection_vs_test: best-epoch bank selected on accumulation split; held-out evaluation
claims.result_denominator: avg held-out 56.17 [54.98, 57.37] vs MemP 53.65 [52.09, 55.20]; per-benchmark margins over best baseline +0.2 to +2.3 pp
claims.counterevidence: CI overlap; margins within SD on LLAB, LiveCodeBench, BFCL; init and tuning confounds on DSBench/AutomationBench.
claims.allowed_conclusion: MemQ is at least on par with and probably modestly above the best baseline on held-out tasks; effect size uncertain.

claims.text: MemQ improves final runtime SR and cumulative SR over MemRL
claims.selection_vs_test: same tasks as used to build memory
claims.result_denominator: avg final SR 71.50 vs 67.27; CSR 78.88 vs 76.75
claims.counterevidence: Training-stream performance, not generalization; CSR is inflated by exploration and re-attempts.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Faster/better in-stream learning than MemRL in these runs.

claims.text: Bootstrapping and multi-depth propagation are what help
claims.result_denominator: eval SR drops of 5.72/8.57 pp (LCB), 2.43/4.41 (BFCL), 3.73/4.88 (DSBench) for gamma=0/lambda=0
claims.counterevidence: Small eval sets; benchmark-dependent optimum; fixed point lambda-independent in theory.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Propagation beyond direct parents contributes in these three tasks.

claims.text: Learned Q-values track success and MemQ keeps more historical coverage; uses fewer tokens
claims.result_denominator: r=0.640 over 480 rollouts; gap CSR-final 1.46 vs 3.16 (Auto), 11.39 vs 14.58 (BFCL); tokens 313M vs 352M (DSBench)
claims.counterevidence: Correlational; differences within SD for tokens.

claims.text: Gains are limited on self-contained multiple-choice tasks
claims.allowed_conclusion: No meaningful gain demonstrated outside multi-step interaction tasks.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a frozen LLM, per-memory Q-values updated by TD(lambda) over the provenance DAG give small but consistent mean improvements in held-out and in-stream success over single-step Q (MemRL) and other memory baselines on five interaction-type benchmarks, and ablating bootstrapping or ancestor propagation lowers success in three of them (author-reported, 3 seeds).
assessment.not_supported: Statistically reliable held-out superiority per benchmark; that ancestor credit reflects causal contribution; benefit independent of initialisation and per-benchmark gamma/lambda tuning; harm removal or store hygiene; gains on self-contained reasoning tasks.
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; not reproduced. Improver level not claimed.

G.reason: Precise residual (ancestor credit in memory-creation chains) against a named closest neighbor (MemRL, run as baseline) with a clear TD lineage; frequency/depth of such chains in the data is not shown, and other memory-utility methods are only cited.

M.reason: EC-MDP formalization, first-order projection with bounded residual, and path-weighted TD(lambda) on a provenance DAG form a coherent, reconstructable response; convergence proof is for fixed DAGs and the fixed point is lambda-independent, exposure edges are not causal, optimistic parent-mean init is a further assumption.

X.reason: Full algorithm, depth cap, pruning floor, clipping, per-benchmark hyperparameter tables and code are given; value-based ranking and epsilon-greedy are specified, but admission is unconditional, nothing is retired or rolled back, and the store only grows.

E.measurement.reason: Benchmark-native success rates with cumulative and final metrics, appropriate No Memory/RAG/MemRL baselines; held-out sets are only 35-150 tasks and the Final SR/CSR headline numbers are measured on the memory-building tasks.

E.causality.reason: Targeted gamma=0, lambda=0, Q-weight and initialisation ablations plus the single-step MemRL baseline isolate the mechanism reasonably; confounded by differing initial Q and extra tuned knobs, no shuffled-provenance or non-DAG control, correlational Q-success evidence, tiny eval sets.

E.holdout.reason: Separate held-out split per benchmark and best epoch selected on accumulation split; no-tuning-on-held-out stated only for LLAB, selection of gamma/lambda elsewhere not described, held-out sets small, runtime headline numbers are not held-out.

E.statistics.reason: Three seeds with mean and SD plus approximate 95% CIs on averages, but no significance tests, margins often inside SD, CIs overlap with the best baseline, ablations reported as point estimates.

E.cost.reason: Token consumption including agent/judge/memory calls reported with SD for MemQ, MemRL, MemP on DSBench and a complexity analysis of path enumeration; only one benchmark, differences within SD, wall-clock of DAG updates not given.
